entries.label: The G-Zero
entries.summary: Major powers turn inward and global governance fails.
entries.quote: In the G-Zero, the world's major powers set aside aspirations for global leadership—alone, coordinated, or otherwise—and look primarily inward for their policy priorities.

entries.label: Europe
entries.summary: Eurozone uncertainty grows though the euro stays intact.
entries.quote: 2011 will be a year of growing uncertainty for Europe. The eurozone will remain intact, but the risk will grow that the crisis will balloon into something unmanageable.

entries.label: Cybersecurity and geopolitics
entries.summary: Cybersecurity becomes a political as well as business risk.
entries.quote: For the past decade, increasingly technologically capable hackers and organized crime organizations have elevated cybersecurity as a business risk, but not as a political risk.

entries.label: China
entries.quote: With a sluggish global recovery, especially in the industrialized countries where unemployment remains high, the China growth story will generate more and more resentment abroad.

entries.label: North Korea
entries.summary: North Korea provokes the South despite Chinese pressure.
entries.quote: In 2011, the North Koreans are likely to take provocative steps against the south despite reasonably strong pressure from China.

entries.label: Capital controls
entries.quote: The risk is rising that a number of countries, including those that resisted the urge last year, will impose capital controls in 2011.

entries.label: US gridlock
entries.summary: Gridlock in Washington becomes a problem.
entries.quote: Strong governance is generally considered good for emerging markets, where new policies are needed to make the trains run on time; while gridlock is a fine outcome for developed states, allowing markets and businesses to prosper undisturbed.

entries.label: Pakistan
entries.summary: Pakistan's internal problems are the main risk in the subcontinent.
entries.quote: The risk in the subcontinent this year isn't Afghanistan-Pakistan (or Af-Pak, as it's called in Washington). It's Pak-Pak.

entries.label: Mexico
entries.quote: 2011 promises to be a very challenging year for Mexico.

entries.label: Emerging markets
entries.summary: Emerging markets diverge and some underperform.
entries.quote: The dramatic increase in the flow of capital into emerging markets has lifted all boats. But there are very different risk profiles among emerging markets, and not all are going to perform well this year.

entries.label: Iran
entries.summary: Eurasia Group sees little need to worry about military strikes on Iran in 2011.
entries.quote: So, there's little need to worry about military strikes.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Turkey
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects no break between Turkey and the West.
entries.quote: Expect more geo-strategic hedging, but no break with the West.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Sudan
entries.summary: Eurasia Group does not expect Sudan to return to civil war.
entries.quote: Despite a great deal of (legitimate) hand-wringing, Sudan's not headed back to civil war.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Nigeria
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects Nigerian politics to stay messy but stable.
entries.quote: Nigeria will continue to prove more resilient than most expect.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

notes: Captured from the archived Eurasia Group page (the undated URL /pages/top-risks, archived 16 January 2011). The page names the G-Zero as the top risk of 2011. Signed 'Ian and David'; the 2010 edition is signed by Ian Bremmer and David Gordon. Publication day not printed on the page.
